Let
\[
s_n=\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_n=1).
\]
By de Finetti’s theorem for infinite exchangeable Bernoulli sequences, there is a random variable \(\Theta\in[0,1]\) such that, conditionally on \(\Theta\), the \(X_i\) are i.i.d. Bernoulli\((\Theta)\). Hence
\[
\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_k=1)=\mathbb E[\Theta^k].
\]
The assumptions give
\[
\mathbb E[\Theta]=p,
\]
and since
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(X_1,X_2)
=\frac{\mathbb P(X_1=X_2=1)-p^2}{p(1-p)},
\]
we also have
\[
\mathbb E[\Theta^2]=\mathbb P(X_1=X_2=1)
=p^2+\rho p(1-p).
\]
Write
\[
m_2=p^2+\rho p(1-p),
\qquad
a=\frac{p-m_2}{1-p}=p(1-\rho).
\]

We must maximize \(\mathbb E[\Theta^n]\) over \(\Theta\in[0,1]\) with first two moments \(p,m_2\).

Consider the quadratic \(Q\) that satisfies
\[
Q(a)=a^n,\qquad Q'(a)=n a^{n-1},\qquad Q(1)=1.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
Q(x)=L(x)+K(x-a)(x-1),
\]
where \(L\) is the line through \((a,a^n)\) and \((1,1)\). Since \(x^n\) has nonnegative third derivative on \([0,1]\), Hermite interpolation gives
\[
Q(x)\ge x^n\qquad(0\le x\le1).
\]
Also,
\[
\mathbb E[(\Theta-a)(\Theta-1)]
=\mathbb E[\Theta^2]-(1+a)\mathbb E[\Theta]+a
=m_2-(1+a)p+a=0,
\]
by the definition of \(a\). Therefore
\[
\mathbb E[\Theta^n]\le \mathbb E[Q(\Theta)]
=\mathbb E[L(\Theta)].
\]
Now
\[
L(x)=a^n+\frac{1-a^n}{1-a}(x-a),
\]
so
\[
\mathbb E[L(\Theta)]
=a^n+\frac{1-a^n}{1-a}(p-a)
=\frac{p-a+(1-p)a^n}{1-a}.
\]
Since \(a=p(1-\rho)\), this upper bound is
\[
\frac{p\rho+(1-p)\bigl(p(1-\rho)\bigr)^n}{1-p(1-\rho)}.
\]

It remains to show this is attainable. Let \(\Theta\) take the two values \(1\) and \(a=p(1-\rho)\), with
\[
\mathbb P(\Theta=1)=\frac{p-a}{1-a}
=\frac{p\rho}{1-p(1-\rho)}.
\]
Then \(\mathbb E[\Theta]=p\), \(\mathbb E[\Theta^2]=m_2\), so the required \(p\) and \(\rho\) are satisfied, and
\[
\mathbb E[\Theta^n]
=\frac{p\rho+(1-p)\bigl(p(1-\rho)\bigr)^n}{1-p(1-\rho)}.
\]

Thus the largest possible value is
\[
\boxed{\frac{p\rho+(1-p)\bigl(p(1-\rho)\bigr)^n}{1-p(1-\rho)}}.
\]
